proposedchanges.title: CPJ Report Warns of Risks to U.S. Press Freedom Ahead of 2024 Election
proposedchanges.description_long: On October 1, 2024, the Committee to Protect Journalists published a report assessing risks facing U.S. journalists before the presidential election. Drawing on interviews and research, CPJ described threats, harassment, arrests, police treatment, and costly legal disputes affecting reporters. The report included unsuccessful defamation suits brought by Donald Trump and his campaign against major news organizations. It also warned that attacks on the press in the United States could influence press freedom abroad, connecting domestic conditions with the example American institutions set internationally. The report assessed risks and reported conditions. It does not establish that Trump led a coordinated decade-long campaign to eliminate press freedom, ordered violence against journalists, or used hundreds of lawsuits to bankrupt media companies. The current long makes those claims without support in the supplied packet. Keep the account focused on CPJ’s findings and distinguish documented legal disputes and reported safety concerns from broader conclusions the report does not prove.

evidencebasis: The packet links to CPJ’s report, and the merged medium identifies its October 1, 2024 publication, research basis, reported issues, unsuccessful defamation suits, and concern about effects abroad. The long still contains the packet’s unsupported allegations. The source URLs are retained.
notes: The press-freedom category and topic tags match the report. Replace the title and long while keeping the medium’s narrower factual account.
